sourceCases.conclusion: One complete native acceptance design is specified; no production native pass or architectural retirement is inferred
sourceCases.missing: Generated normal-path static/generic fixtures, independent operand/slot oracle and coherent native cohort remain absent.
sourceCases.acceptance: Cases and independent observations in the existing request-service design; whole five-gate and original-load closure remain required
sourceCases.formalBoundary: Existing interrupt_request_lifecycle waitServiceEntry/waitRepark/waitControlSafe own temporal cardinality; Lean alone owns slots/aliases/intervals. These source/native oracle premises add no duplicate proof.
sourceCases.counterexample: A double-restore callback exits before the old queue path, or a public immediate lock test never enters the generated wait corridor.

sourceCases.counterexample: Cumulative inserts exceed one legitimately, but two live arms or deadline reset are accepted; alternatively legitimate rearm is incorrectly forbidden.

sourceBindings.observed: current-frame/context->frame freeze current slots/regs/closed with supplied live set. gen-call chooses specialized/inlinable procedure handling; gen-return-label adjoins result-var and attaches that frame to generated return labels/jumps.
sourceBindings.required: Recognize only admitted completion semantics in gen-call/role lowering, preserve argument evaluation/reason/tail/result behavior, and make future static decode/exposure real semantic uses before current-frame is attached. A hidden runtime use or metadata annotation alone cannot keep M0 live.
sourceBindings.gap: No S frontend role/effect lowering exists. Generic helper fallback, ordinary Scheme return values and proper tail behavior cannot be inferred from a backend bitmap edit.
sourceBindings.question: SH-CUT-S

sourceBindings.observed: GVM frame stores size/slots/regs/closed/live. frame-live? keeps closure-env-var when any closed variable is live. Target instruction scanning takes entry/exit frames from attached GVM metadata; merely deleting a C closure allocation does not recompute that semantic state.
sourceBindings.required: Introduce S lexical snapshot, caller link, return/retry roles and all snapshot temporaries before semantic liveness freezes; propagate them through actual GVM frames and then physical FrameSpec. Preserve alias semantics and control behavior, not old numeric slots.
sourceBindings.gap: No S semantic lowering exists; inherited closure-env liveness, saved-register maps and raw exposure may still require original roots. No register-deadness claim follows from a minimal frame bitmap.
sourceBindings.question: SH-CUT-S

sourceBindings.observed: Normal return derives fs, ret-var link and live-slot map. Internal check return extends aligned slots with saved GVM registers and marks all saved registers live. Debug-info-add! has a separate queued side effect later consumed by debug-info-generate; its ignored helper parameter does not prove debug data lost.
sourceBindings.required: Separate S saved layout, check RETI extension and final return/result maps. Maintain exact slot/ret-var/debug-label correspondence for every generated point; no constant fs guess or bitmap-only root proof.
sourceBindings.gap: Proposed S/check/final-return frames and debug logical projection are not generated or round-trip-qualified; declaration validation is not liveness completeness.
sourceBindings.question: SH-CUT-S

sourceBindings.observed: FrameSpec validates kind, stored/actual fs, link and bitmap bounds; internal size expansion differs from normal. Inline versus out-of-line metadata and gcmap chunks are emitted from this one spec.
sourceBindings.required: Compute S reserve, ordinary/structural slots and every checkpoint from one semantic plan. Size validity, code/module lifetime, field schema and stale native-module admission are distinct requirements. No minimal two-slot or zero reserve overhead assumption.
sourceBindings.gap: S descriptors, admission record and old-metadata rejection are proposed; source byte equality does not supply a regenerated GCC/C23 producer.
sourceBindings.question: SH-CUT-S

sourceBindings.observed: Park/restore lowering runs end-of-block checks and adjusts stack before emitted root macros.
sourceBindings.required: Make all selected source/destination/conversion operands semantically live before checks, reload repaired roots and preserve exact normal/RETI maps.
sourceBindings.gap: No typed post-registration conversion/query lowering exists.

sourceBindings.observed: Park writes break.next and Thread.cont.frame then invokes callback; neither root store is wait-registration commit.
sourceBindings.required: Retain complete source/destination roots through real source freeze; publish executable conversion only after roots and same-wait authority.
sourceBindings.gap: No same-wait receipt/query is supplied by existing macro stores.

sourceBindings.required: ACK target must bind repaired active/break/captured ancestry and survive next roster, not depend on the cleared wrapper.
sourceBindings.gap: No conversion ACK or last-user proof follows from restore macro.

sourceBindings.observed: Wake removes queues, sets actual ownership or abandonment and fixed resume outcome, then publishes runnable Thread.
sourceBindings.required: Conversion revalidates same physical wait and selected outcome under existing locks; no replay/overwriting grant with stale retry.
sourceBindings.gap: Current registration fields have no atomic conversion receipt/query.

sourceBindings.observed: Dispatcher caches resume-thunk before draining arbitrary interrupts and invokes cached local afterward.
sourceBindings.required: Cover the cached action as actual rooted last user and preserve invocation/outcome semantics through conversion, reflection and GC.
sourceBindings.gap: Changing Thread.resume-thunk alone does not revoke local alias or prove old graph retirement.

sourceBindings.observed: Thread end removes queues, clears continuation/denv/cache, and does not establish death of user-captured frames or cached action.
sourceBindings.required: Retain unresolved source/destination and query records with existing VM/source custody until actual last users/writers drain; fresh user shot needs fresh physical authority.
sourceBindings.gap: No current conversion exit/reader retirement implementation is qualified.

sourceBindings.observed: Current helper has three physical outcomes: immediate acquisition, immediate timeout, or queue insertion with resume publication and scheduling; the general caller still captures and builds recursive resume.
sourceBindings.required: Separate admission before first registration from recovery of an existing registration; late fallback preserves the selected grant/timeout/abandon outcome. After proven service withdrawal, an unsatisfied durable wait may rearm through the helper under a fresh physical arm of the same logical wait; unknown completion cannot authorize blind reinsertion.
sourceBindings.gap: No production typed same-wait conversion/recovery landing is emitted. Source helper existence is not capture elimination.

sourceBindings.observed: Restored captured callback exits through a fresh escape before the old physical queue path. Two-shot graph/winding/alias checks are real but do not execute production wait conversion.
sourceBindings.required: Retain this graph control and separately exercise generated normal wait completion, timeout, abandonment and post-registration fallback without the escape landing before claiming production closure.
sourceBindings.gap: Original workload, production static entry and independent final result oracle remain unexecuted/unimplemented.

sourceBindings.observed: Interrupt propagation removes existing BTQ and TOQ membership before making the target runnable; a service wake is not a terminal mutex grant.

sourceBindings.gap: No production arm receipt or independent canonical queue membership probe is qualified.

scenarios.oracle: Actual target wait -> queue -> real grant -> normal return marker -> natural join; no early escape
Force helper recheck branch separately from public fast-path bypass
Original deadline or legal owner termination; preserve #f versus abandoned exception
Known old arm withdrawal -> service/GC -> predicate unsatisfied -> one next arm
Consume durable predicate or already selected grant without stale retry
Exposure/reserve failure -> same-key settlement; UNKNOWN never authorizes blind reinsertion
Hold cached/query user through ACK and owner exit; repair target next W<R GC before last-user retirement
Two admitted real user shots across GC; each passes actual wait return marker before controller transfer
Generic once only before first arm; after entry preserve roots/debt and explicit UNKNOWN

correctedPremises.physicalRegistration: At most one simultaneous arm, not one cumulative insertion per logical wait. Query never rearms; known withdrawal plus predicate/deadline recheck may authorize the next arm.
correctedPremises.marginalCaptureCost: Checked Scheme captures once per real mutex-wait entry; subsequent resume reuses wait. Rearm count cannot multiply capture savings.
correctedPremises.observerEffect: Target continuation capture is interrupt service exposure, not passive observation. Lack of a benchmark observer does not prove closed-world eligibility.
correctedPremises.pbtScope: Current serial overridden RC trial and generic -:p1 child do not qualify concurrent R3/W2 production queue histories.
